title: ExSASCA: Exact Soft Analytical Side-Channel Attacks using Tractable Circuits
description:
Experimental code for ExSASCA, a fast and exact probabilistic inference method for soft analytical side-channel attacks (SASCA) on the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES), based on knowledge compilation and tractable probabilistic circuits.

The state-of-the-art SASCA uses physical leakage information to make probabilistic predictions about intermediate computations and combines these guesses with the known algorithmic logic to compute the posterior distribution over the key. This attack is commonly performed via loopy belief propagation, which lacks guarantees in terms of convergence and inference quality. ExSASCA instead performs exact inference by compiling the AES MixColumns relation into a Sentential Decision Diagram (SDD). When attacking AES, ExSASCA outperforms SASCA by more than 31% top-1 success rate absolute, at little more computational cost, and about 3 orders of magnitude less than exact inference via exhaustive enumeration.

This archive contains the CNF encoding and SDD compilation pipeline for AES MixColumns, the ExSASCA inference implementation, the compiled SDD artifacts, and the scripts reproducing the experiments of the accompanying ICML 2024 paper.
